reviewer: Round-2 Reviewer #1 — Degree-requirements audit (ASU BA General Studies, LSGNSBGS, ASU Online/CISA). Live search was unavailable (session WebSearch budget exhausted at 200/200; fetch blocked), so every judgement below rests on the scout briefs plus catalog knowledge; confidence is tagged per item.
verdict: REVISE BEFORE EXECUTION. Credit arithmetic is exact (12 + 12 + 42 + 42 + 21.334 + 21 = 150.334; ULC 10x3 + 3x4 = 42 with 13 courses, not 14) and the union covers every General Studies Gold bucket, FYC and four topic areas on paper. But the union as drafted contains three duplicate-credit collisions that ASU will post only once (BYU POLI 110 vs ULC POS 110; HES PHYS E-1bx vs BYU PHSCS 106; ULC ECN 212 vs UMPI ECO 208 with BYU ECON 110 overlapping both), which would silently drop the audit below 150.334; the IDS 321 / IDS 402 substitutes are double-assigned across three plans; no ASU 101 substitute is actually scheduled; UCLA ENVIRON X 400 is post-baccalaureate professional credit that ASU is unlikely to accept; and the 45-credit upper-division minimum is met only if every uncertain item (HES level, UCLA XL 115A availability, BYU ENGL 316 availability, X 400 acceptance) breaks the right way (secure UD = 36 of 45). Applying the nine swaps below fixes all of this while keeping every school's total exact (12 / 12 / 42 / 42 / 21.334 / 21) and moves cost from about $36,129 to about $36,154.

notes:
Assumptions stated: (1) ASU Online's 'three classes from each of four topic areas' is treated as mandatory for all four areas; the student's two theme labels are mapped to official areas as follows — 'Technology & Government' = Area 3 (National and civil service and professional studies) + Area 4 (Organizations, technology and ethics); 'Socio-Technical Systems: Energy & Environment' = Area 1 (Global and natural science perspectives); Area 2 (Humanities, identities and society) is filled with cheap UMPI/BYU/ULC humanities. (2) Placement of transfer courses into topic areas and level assignment for HES courses are CISA decisions; ULC natives are the only risk-free anchors, so the revised plan keeps at least one ULC course in every area (POS 110, SOS 100/PHY 194, HST 102, CIS 308). (3) A course used as an IDS 321/IDS 402 substitute is not also counted as a cluster course. (4) Under Gold, one course is applied to only one Gold requirement (verify with CISA; if double-use is allowed, the plan simply gains slack). (5) ASU 101 is assumed waived for a transfer admit; the plan names ULC TEL 111 as the contingency substitute and the ULC RAS 210 slot as the flexible native plug for any Gold designation that fails to attach by transfer. (6) Residency ignored per user; the 42 ULC credits would satisfy it anyway.

Revised union after the swaps (credits exact): ULC 42 = ENG 101, CIS 105, MAT 265 (in progress), ENG 102, POS 110, SOS 100, CHM 114 (4), RAS 210, PHY 194, HST 102, BIO 100 (4), CIS 308, AST 111 (4) — 13 courses, $5,525. SNHU 12 = SCI-220, IDS-401 (IDS 321 sub), MAT-350, IDS-403 (IDS 402 sub, last) — $4,248. HES 12 = GOVT E-1820, CSCI E-45b, ENVR E-101 — $6,780 (2027-28 increase not budgeted). UCLA 21.334 = COM SCI XL 31, MATH XL 61, MATH XL 31B, ECON XL 2, MATH XL 32A, MATH XL 33A, MATH XL 33B, MATH XL 115A — ~$8,825. BYU 21 = POLI 170, HIST 201, PHSCS 105, STAT 121, PHSCS 106, GEOG 120, ENGL 316 — $5,376. Grand total 150.334 (ASU posting ~150.33); cost ~$36,154 at 2026 list prices. Upper-division after swaps: secure 39 (ULC 3, SNHU 9, UMPI 27) + HES 8 + BYU 3 + UCLA 2.665 = up to 52.7 against the 45 minimum; cluster UD 23 against 18. Duplicate-equivalency check after swaps: POS 110 once (ULC), POS 160 once (BYU POLI 170), PHY 111/112 once each (BYU), ECN 211 once (UCLA), ECN 212 once (UMPI), CSE 100 once (UCLA), HST 100/102/110 once each, PHI 101 once (UMPI), PSY none, STP 226 once (BYU), MAT 266/267/343/275 once each (UCLA, MAT-350 posts as MAT 3XX elective).
